title: Stop a declared test command from silently unscoping three roles

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 9341cc9 with bookkeeping afdec15, main checkout. Sprint file read fresh. Working tree clean apart from the known .vscode file.

This sprint's whole job is correcting claims that overstated what evidence reached. Every correction is accurate and I checked each against the code or the record rather than accepting it.

================================================================
REQ 1 — MET, AND IT HALF-CLOSES AN ITEM I RAISED IN SPRINT 17
================================================================

The comment now reads: sprint 17 confirmed by running that a trailing ` *` pattern also matches the bare command with no arguments -- "but only for git, a real verb, in a real push. The equivalent npm case was proxied by an `npm pack` request that Pipeman declined as outside its own process, so no permission decision for a bare `npm` was ever actually reached. Confirmed: git. Inferred, not established: npm and every other entry on this list -- this comment used to claim both on the evidence of one."

It does not generalise from one verb; it names the one verb, names why the second case never produced a decision, and labels the rest inferred. That is the criterion's own test passed.

Worth recording for my own carried items: this is the sprint 17 question I left open ("does `Bash(npm publish *)` match a bare `npm publish`?"). It is now answered for git and explicitly unanswered for npm, which is the honest state. The open item narrows rather than closing — a bare `npm publish` is still an inference, and it is still the one irreversible command in this framework. Keep it on the list.

================================================================
REQ 2 — MET, DECISION RECORDED, MATCHER UNTOUCHED
================================================================

The decision is recorded and it went the way that keeps the mechanism honest: instruct roles not to append shell chaining rather than widening the matcher. Verified by rendering the real prompts rather than reading the source — "Do not append shell chaining like ; echo $? or && echo done." is present, and present for all six roles, not just the one I sampled.

The matcher itself is untouched: filtering the entire run-role.js diff for non-comment, non-blank changes returns EMPTY. Every change to that file this sprint is a comment. That is exactly what "the matcher's single-command behaviour itself untouched" has to mean, and it is checkable rather than asserted.

================================================================
REQ 3 — MET, AND THE INSTRUCTION IS NOT WEAKENED
================================================================

The criterion warns that a weakened instruction is a defect — roles still need to write notes inside the working directory. Checked all three files: the working-directory instruction is intact in qa1.md, liveqa.md and sprint-new.md. What changed is the attribution, now "a property of those two mechanisms specifically" (shell redirects and the Write tool) rather than of the profile or session generally. Corrected without softening the operational advice, which was the hard part.

The four-legs enumeration in run-role.js is the right replacement for "directory confinement," and the fourth leg is what makes it honest: legs 1-3 are named as real checkable properties, leg 4 is named as a trust decision and not a sandbox. Adding `Bash(git push *)` as an explicitly enumerated leg is a genuine improvement even though nothing changed behaviourally — verified the disallow list still literally contains it (`OWNED_REPOSITORY_DISALLOWED_TOOLS = ['Bash(git push *)']`), so the enumeration matches the code rather than describing an intention.

================================================================
REQ 4 — READ COLD. IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ALL FIVE.
================================================================

Rule 6 (commit an amendment before handing it to a gate) is written against the right moment: "commit then, not 'eventually, whenever a sprint next gets committed for an unrelated reason.'" I tested it against the instances I personally hit: sprint 11's rescope, sprint 14's line-38 correction, sprint 19's authorization amendment, and sprint 19's four-controls correction were all uncommitted when handed to me, and I held the verdict on each for exactly the reason this rule now states. It would have caught every one. It also states the consequence correctly — a verdict against a working-tree file is one the durable history cannot back up.

Rule 7 (the companion) is the better of the two, because it names a failure mode nobody had articulated: recording an absorption in Dependencies while leaving the requirement live in Requirements and Acceptance Criteria. And it extends itself to the smaller version — "a stale requirement number left in a Risks bullet is a smaller version of the same half-edit."

================================================================
FOR MASTER CONTROLLER — THE SPRINT FILE CURRENTLY VIOLATES THE RULE IT IS INTRODUCING
================================================================

Dev Team flagged this and correctly did not touch a sprint file. I verified it independently rather than relaying:

  Out of Scope, first bullet: "Req 3 decides only whether roles are told to work with it."
  The compound-command decision is Req 2. Req 3 is the retire-"directory-confined" requirement.
  Risks & Mitigations carries the same shifted numbering.

Rule 7, added by this sprint, covers this case in terms: clear the stale references in the same edit. So sprint 18 is shipping a rule against half-edits in a file that contains one.

I am not blocking on it. It is Master Controller's file, Dev Team cannot fix it, and it does not affect the build or my verdict — I audited against the Acceptance Criteria section, whose numbering is current and matched what I checked. But it should be cleaned before this closes, for two reasons beyond tidiness: the rule's own credibility depends on the file that introduces it, and a future reader reconciling Risks against Requirements will hit the exact confusion rule 7 exists to prevent.

Sequencing, since it has cost a round three times now: amending the sprint file after this PASS changes qa1_audit_file_hash and /sprint-dev-done will refuse. Decide it deliberately rather than meeting it at dev-done.

================================================================
REQS 5, 6 — MET
================================================================

Req 5 — package.json 0.1.20, one line, and 0.1.19 confirmed live before bumping.
Req 6 — ran it: 171 OK, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED; ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; verify-tarball.sh PASSED, "Installed 0.1.20 (first install)". The new test asserts Req 2's instruction is present for every role, which is the right assertion — a per-role check rather than a sample. Declining to add tests for the prose-only requirements, and saying so, is what Req 6 asked for rather than a gap.

INFORMATIONAL

1. The commit-splitting note in the handoff (a local `git reset --soft` to separate build from bookkeeping before anything was pushed or reviewed) is the right way to fix that and the right thing to disclose. Nothing was rewritten that anyone had seen.
2. Carried, unchanged: the bare-`npm publish` inference above; the CLI-version-drift item, still the strongest-evidenced open item and still unscheduled; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration falling through silently; the --agents argv budget against Windows' 32,767-char limit.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it, once Master Controller decides on the stale numbering. /sprint-dev-done 18, then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.20, then `verify-publish 18`.

Worth saying once: three of this sprint's six requirements exist because a comment claimed more than its evidence reached, and two of those were claims I flagged in earlier audits. This sprint is the epic turning around and fixing its own record rather than only its code, and the rules it adds are the first ones aimed at the artifact rather than the build.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.1.20 against scratch repos on macOS. Environment: macOS Darwin arm64, claude 2.1.259. 2026-09-05. ~$0.62 in billed runs.

All four criteria pass. Two of them were open questions I had failed to settle at earlier gates, and both are now closed by observation rather than inference — which was the entire point of how they were worded.

PROVENANCE
0.1.20 on the registry; gitHead 527760799bf160135393960a7017a644a77a660a == last_shipped_commit; zero `reshipped` events; QA1 PASS round 1. Content check per sprint 13's rule: all 57 published files byte-identical to `git show 5277607:<path>`, MISMATCHED 0, tarball sha1 matches the registry's dist.shasum. Own registry query run before reading verify-publish's record.

================================================================
CRITERION — THE HONEST DECLARATION STILL WORKS: PASS
================================================================
Downstream scratch project, its own package.json and test suite, `fullyCompletely.testCommand: "npm test"`, NO ownership declaration (so the narrow/default profile). Complete sprint spec.

  src/format.js written by the role: YES
  the project's own test command:    "tests passed"
  permission denials:                0
  11 turns, exit 0, $0.20

Sprint 17's mechanism is intact on 0.1.20: a project declares its own test command, the role runs the target's tests, nothing is denied because nothing outside the declaration was needed.

================================================================
CRITERION — FORCE A DENIAL ON DEV-TEAM: FORCED. THE BOUND IS NOW OBSERVED, NOT INSPECTED.
================================================================
This is the criterion I failed at sprint 17 and again at sprint 19, both times recording plainly that I could not force one. It is now forced.

Same downstream shape, narrow profile, `testCommand: "npm test"` — but the spec's first requirement legitimately needs `npm install`, which `Bash(npm test *)` does not cover:

  DENIED Bash : npm install 2>&1 | tail -50
  DENIED Bash : npm install
  Status: BLOCKED - sprint aborted. No commit was made - nothing was built.
  left-pad installed: no
  2 denials, 17 turns, exit 0

The role hit the bound, reported it, and did NOT work around it — it did not hand-write a substitute for the dependency, which the spec's own Risks section had told it not to do. So the narrow profile's bound is real, observable, and the role's behaviour at the bound is correct.

WHY MY TWO EARLIER ATTEMPTS FAILED, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. At sprint 17 I asked pipeman to run an ad-hoc `npm pack`; it declined as outside its process. At sprint 19 I embedded "run `git log --oneline -5`" as a sprint requirement; dev-team-2 identified it as an instruction aimed at the agent inside inert sprint data and refused. Both times the role's own judgment stopped it BEFORE the permission layer was ever consulted, so no permission decision existed to observe. The method that works is to give the role a task it genuinely needs the missing tool for, as part of its actual job. Then it reaches for the tool honestly and the bound answers.

Recording that because "I could not force a denial" appeared in two of my reports as a limitation, and it was a limitation of my method rather than of the bound.

================================================================
CRITERION — THE NPM VERB: ESTABLISHED, NO LONGER INFERRED
================================================================
Open since sprint 17, where my proxy went through pipeman and was declined before any permission decision was reached. Req 1 correctly recorded the state of the evidence as "Confirmed: git. Inferred, not established: npm."

The safe route sprint 17 lacked is to test the matcher directly rather than through a role that will decline on process grounds. Ran claude with the single relevant entry and nothing else:

  claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Bash(npm pack *)"
  task: run exactly `npm pack`, nothing appended, no arguments, no redirect
  RESULT: permission_denials 0, and bare-verb-probe-1.0.0.tgz was produced

The tarball is the part that matters: it proves the bare command actually RAN, rather than merely not being denied. `npm pack` was chosen because it is the one npm verb that writes only a local tarball and touches no registry — the reason the equivalent test with `npm publish` was correctly never attempted, by Dev Team or by me.

So `Bash(<verb> *)` matches a genuinely bare invocation for npm as well as for git. Two real verbs now, not one and an inference.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHIPPED COMMENT, AND IT IS A GOOD ONE: run-role.js:1016-1024 currently reads "Confirmed: git. Inferred, not established: npm and every other entry on this list." That was accurate when written and is now understated for npm specifically. Whoever next opens that file can promote npm from inferred to confirmed and cite this gate. The broader caveat — that every OTHER entry on the list remains inferred — stays true and should stay.

================================================================
THE PROSE CORRECTIONS, VERIFIED IN THE SHIPPED PACKAGE
================================================================
Req 3, "directory-confined" retired: ZERO occurrences anywhere in the published package. This was my sprint-19 directive and it has been acted on completely rather than partially.

Req 1, the two-verbs-on-one-verb's-evidence claim: corrected. The comment now names what was confirmed (git, in a real push), what was attempted and why it produced nothing (the `npm pack` request pipeman declined as outside its process), and what remains inferred. It states the evidence rather than the conclusion.

Req 4, Master Controller commits amendments before handing to a gate: present in the shipped `.claude/agents/master-controller.md`, with the five instances named (sprints 11, 14, 19 twice, and sprint 19's round-3 authorization record) and the reason stated — "a verdict recorded against an uncommitted working-tree file is a verdict the durable history can't actually back up". That is the right framing: it is about what the record can support, not about tidiness.

Req 2, the compound-command cost: decided rather than omitted. run-role.js:689 records it as "a separate, larger problem, deliberately left there rather than folded in here." The requirement said either answer is fine and deciding by omission is not; a named deferral with a reason is a decision.

Req 6, tests only where warranted: isBareInterpreter's coverage is intact and I re-ran its behaviour directly at sprint 19's gate.

================================================================
NOT MY CALL, ACKNOWLEDGED NOT ACTED ON
================================================================
QA1's observation that the sprint file introducing the amendment rule itself carries the exact half-edit pattern that rule exists to catch, in its own Risks and Out-of-Scope sections. Pipeman passed it along explicitly as Master Controller's timing call and not something for my live test. I have not checked it, have not scored it, and am recording only that it was received and left alone. Fixing it now would force a fresh audit before dev-done, which is a real cost and a reasonable thing to defer deliberately.

================================================================
WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
================================================================
Every result here I produced directly on macOS against the published 0.1.20. Provenance was established by my own registry query and a full content comparison before reading verify-publish's record. Pipeman's report arrived mid-run and changed nothing.

The npm-verb result and the forced denial are both first-time observations rather than confirmations of someone else's claim, and both close questions that earlier reports of mine had left explicitly open.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================
Ship-ready. This is a small sprint that did what small sprints should: it corrected two claims that were stronger than their evidence, retired a phrase that had become misleading, and added the missing workflow step behind five recurring instances — without inventing tests for prose.

Nothing carries forward as a defect. One item is now better than the release states: npm's bare-verb behaviour is established rather than inferred, and the comment recording it can be upgraded next time that file is open. The remaining entries on that allowlist stay inferred and the comment's caveat about them should not be weakened.

This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 18.
